part.text:
The issue is fixed. All tests pass (267 total, 0 failures), and manual verification confirms correct behavior.

**Root cause:** In `src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs`, `--plain` had `.overrides_with("paging")` and `--paging` had `.overrides_with("plain")`. Clap's last-arg-wins override meant `bat --paging=never --plain` silently discarded the explicit `--paging=never`, falling back to auto mode (which pages on an interactive terminal).

**Fix:**
- `src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs`: removed the mutual overrides between `plain` and `paging`, so a single `-p`/`--plain` only affects style while an explicit `--paging=<mode>` is always honored (and vice versa).
- `src/bin/bat/app.rs:248`: since `-pp` must still disable paging when it follows `--paging=always` (existing tests), added order-aware logic: if `plain` count > 1 and its last occurrence comes after an explicitly-set `--paging`, the pager is disabled. Otherwise the existing resolution applies unchanged (`-P`/`--no-paging` and `--paging` keep their clap-level last-wins override).

Verified behaviors:
- `--paging=never --plain` → no paging (reported bug) ✓
- `--paging=always --plain` → pager runs, plain style ✓
- `--paging=always -pp` → no pager ✓ / `-pp --paging=always` → pager ✓
- `--paging=always -P` / `-P --paging=always` → last one wins ✓
